expected_effects: At least 10 percent lower runtime or time-to-95-HV than the initial incumbent at equal NFE
More environmental-selection cycles and higher normalized-HV AUC
No mean final normalized-HV loss greater than 0.005 after intermediate evidence
falsification_evidence: Quick runtime improvement below 10 percent without at least 1 percent normalized-HV/AUC gain
Any development-instance final normalized-HV loss above 0.02
Intermediate mean normalized-HV loss above 0.005 or IGD+ regression above 5 percent without compensating locked efficiency acceptance
novelty: Controlled replacement of SFMO's sequential multi-behavior cycle by an energy-budgeted individual one-shot state decision, expressed as sheep grazing/migration/regrouping rather than a generic operator mixture.
observed_weakness: The scalar SFMO smoke used 648 NFE for only 48 nominal grazing trials, and the protected MO-SFMO repeats up to 20 grazing batches plus migration batches before switching state; its 2000-NFE diagnostic ZDT1 normalized HV was zero.
possible_downsides: Shallower local exploitation can reduce final precision
One-shot switching probabilities can overuse migration on multimodal problems
More frequent archive sorting may consume some of the saved runtime
proposed_modification: For every active sheep and generation, select exactly one of grazing, collective migration, or regrouping from its stagnation state; generate and evaluate exactly one offspring, then perform one population/archive update. Retain N=100, fixed baseline step schedules, external archive, constraints, and no success-history adaptation.
suspected_mechanism: Sequentially executing multiple costly behaviors for every sheep consumes most of the fixed NFE before population-level environmental feedback can change behavior, while repeated migration can amplify the imbalance unpredictably.

expected_effects: Reduce C001 runtime by at least 50 percent
Retain at least 90 percent of C001's normalized-HV gain over baseline
Satisfy the locked runtime non-inferiority threshold against baseline or achieve the locked efficiency acceptance route
falsification_evidence: Quick runtime is not at least 50 percent lower than C001
Quick normalized-HV gain over baseline falls below 0.01
Any development-instance normalized-HV loss relative to baseline exceeds 0.02
Intermediate runtime remains more than 10 percent slower than baseline without an accepted efficiency trade-off
novelty: A biologically interpretable intermittent rumination/social-sharing schedule couples one-shot behavior to computationally sparse archive maintenance; C001 supplies the required one-shot-only ablation.
observed_weakness: C001 reduced intermediate IGD+ to 28.4 percent of baseline and raised mean normalized HV by 0.102, but took 4.33 times the baseline runtime because it performed full population ranking, leader-density calculation, and archive sorting every 100 evaluations.
possible_downsides: Stale leaders can slow response to new sparse-front discoveries
Per-sheep scalar buffering can discard mutually nondominated trials
Five-cycle communication may reduce feasibility propagation on DAS-CMOP
proposed_modification: Reconstruct one-shot switching from the protected baseline but add a rumination buffer: each sheep retains its best trial for five cycles, the external archive and rank chain refresh only at that social interval or final budget, and cached leaders/order guide intervening cycles. This is evaluated against both baseline and the C001 ablation.
suspected_mechanism: Sheep do not communicate every grazing observation to the full flock immediately; retaining each sheep's best recent forage cue and sharing it only at intermittent social pauses should preserve useful one-shot discoveries while reducing O(A^2) archive and ranking work.

expected_effects: Reduce C002 runtime by at least 55 percent
Achieve runtime no more than 1.10 times baseline
Retain at least 90 percent of C002's normalized-HV gain
falsification_evidence: Quick normalized-HV gain over baseline falls below 0.01
Any development-instance normalized-HV loss relative to baseline exceeds 0.02
novelty: The mechanism models flock-wide perception as one shared scent field while serving as a controlled computational ablation of C002.
observed_weakness: C002 retained a 2.55-fold mean normalized-HV ratio and reduced mean IGD+ to 28.7 percent of baseline, but remained 2.46 times slower despite sparse archive refresh.
possible_downsides: Vectorized tie handling could alter trajectories if it does not exactly mirror scalar constrained selection
Shared scent probabilities may reduce guide diversity if archive edge weights dominate
proposed_modification: Retain C002 one-shot switching and five-cycle rumination, but vectorize constrained scalarized replacement for all sheep and sample all archive guides from one crowding-derived probability field per social pause.
suspected_mechanism: A flock reacts to a shared scent and visual field rather than independently recomputing the entire social landscape for every sheep. Computing archive crowding once per pause and applying selection to the flock as arrays should remove interpreter overhead without changing the behavioral trajectory class.
